messages:
emma: Heads-up, seeing a spike in GPU attach failures in us-east1 around 03:12UTC. Correlates with NVMe error bursts on ephemeral drives.

emma: Example from node gnode-1972: kernel logs show long `dm-crypt` waits and `read retry` followed by `block layer timeout`. This lines up with janitor scrub starting.
```
[03:12:08] blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 123456789
[03:12:09] dm-crypt: waiting for crypt request completion (kthread blocked)
[03:12:10] nvme0: I/O 0 QID 1 timeout, aborting
```

raj: ugh. we've seen janitor scrubs + dm-crypt + KMS calls thrash the IOPS before. is this the same encryption key-per-volume flow? :thinking_face:

emma: yes — we use ebs-like LUKS with KMS unwrap on attach. Key unwrap requests spike when janitor/cleaner re-creates ephemeral volumes, and that adds latency to block init paths. GPUs wait on block ready and time out provisioning.

mike: can we cache unwraps in the node agent for short TTL instead of hitting KMS on every attach? that should cut the key call rate.

sara: even with caching, the crypt layer still adds CPU and IOPS overhead on small random reads. we saw read-amplification when scrub walks many small files. Janitor's scrub is too aggressive during batch window.

janitor-bot: scheduled janitor-scrub job started on pool-ephemeral-us-east1 at 03:11:58 (run id: scrub-20260321-07). Throttling: disabled.

raj: janitor-bot unhelpful :grimacing: — can we throttle the scrub concurrency? set to `--max-concurrency=4` instead of 16 for the region during peak GPU allocation windows.

emma: temporary mitigation: 1) throttle janitor concurrency 2) bump kube-affinity so new GPU pods avoid nodes with active scrub 3) add short LRU cache for KMS unwrap per node (ttl 60s)

mike: +1 to caching. also propose switching dm-crypt cipher to `xts-plain64` with hardware crypto offload on supported hosts to reduce CPU. will need kernel config check.

sara: note about risk: changing cipher or offload touches compatibility for snapshot/restore flows. need a canary.

emma: doing a quick canary: patching janitor nodegroup policy in us-east1 to `--max-concurrency=3` now. will monitor GPU attach success and iops.

ops-bot: incident created: INC-2026-0331 (nvme-kms-io-throttle-us-east1). Severity: P2.

mike: I'm going to draft a small node-agent change to cache unwraps and add metrics for KMS QPS and unwrap latencies. will open PR and link here.

sara: also let's add an alert for local block device ioctl latency > 200ms per node for >5m. we have no metric for that currently.

emma: agree. adding ticket for block-latency alert. assigning to @sara.

emma: quick numbers from the last 30m: janitor concurrency=16 -> avg nvme IOPS per node jumped from 12k -> 42k, dm-crypt syscall wait p95 ~ 340ms, GPU-attach failures went from 0.4% -> 6.2% during the window.

raj: cost note: caching unwraps will slightly increase long-lived key material in memory but will reduce KMS egress costs. moving to hardware crypto may increase instance SKU dependency and cost. we should capture tradeoffs.

mike: rough plan & owners:
- throttle janitor (emma) - in progress
- node-agent KMS unwrap cache + metrics (mike) - PR by EOD
- block-latency alert (sara) - ticket created
- canary dm-crypt hw-offload (emma+mike) - schedule tomorrow

sara: ping on PR + add a small perf-run after deploy (run janitor at 0.5x) — we need before/after IOPS and attach success rates.

emma: ack. will update this thread with numbers. thanks all :thumbsup:

ops-bot: update: scrub-20260321-07 paused on 6 nodes by ops (reason: attach errors).

mike: FYI I'll include a small config change example for caching:
```yaml
node-agent:
  kms_unwrap_cache_ttl_seconds: 60
  kms_max_parallel_unwraps: 4
```

emma: looks good. will monitor till 04:00UTC and then roll out node-agent change if stable.

sara: noted — marking followups in INC-2026-0331.
